results.title: Unemployment rate
results.description: The percentage of the labor force that is unemployed and actively seeking employment. It is calculated as the number of unemployed persons divided by the total labor force. A measure that expresses the frequency of occurrence of an event or phenomenon in relation to another quantity.
results.indicator: Unemployment rate

results.title: Gross domestic product (GDP), Current prices, Domestic currency
results.description: Gross domestic product reflects the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach.  Values expressed without any adjustment for price changes Currency issued by the country of origin, used internally. Used to specify what Unit of Measure the country used to provide data to the IMF.�
results.indicator: Gross domestic product (GDP), Current prices, Domestic currency

results.title: All Items, Consumer price index (CPI), Period average, percent change
results.description: All items in the context of the consumer price index indicates that the index includes prices for all items included in the consumer price index basket.  This includes prices related to food, beverages, clothing, housing, health, transport, communications, recreation, education, restaurants and hotels and other miscellanoues goods and services. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is an index of the prices of consumption goods and services, as compared to a certain reference period. This calculates the change relative to the average value over the entire period, not just the starting point. This is often used when the data fluctuates significantly within the period, and the average provides a more representative value for comparison. A ratio expressed as a fraction of 100.
results.indicator: All Items, Consumer price index (CPI), Period average, percent change

dataset.dataflow_description: The World Economic Outlook (WEO) database is created during the biannual WEO exercise, which begins in January and June of each year and results in the April and September/October WEO publication. Selected series from the publication are available in a database format.
